SMTO-EXE-0273 — Web browsing is turned off on this Gateway

GUID: a7eafe92-6d52-5f81-afb7-0ed35f68b69f
Slug: browser-disabled
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: browser

What happened

  • The person who set up this Gateway, the helper program SMTO uses to run things on a computer, turned off its web browser. SMTO can't open websites there, and allowing it in this conversation doesn't change that.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you have another Gateway, select Controls below the message box, choose that Gateway in the Gateway list, then ask again. Browsing is turned off only on this Gateway, so another Gateway may be able to open the website.
  2. Ask the person who manages this Gateway to turn its web browser back on and restart it when no tasks are running on it. The switch is in that computer's Gateway settings, which you can't change from the conversation.
  3. After they restart it, start a new task and ask SMTO to open the website. A task keeps the Gateway's abilities as they were when it started, so only a new task sees the change.

What success looks like

  • SMTO opens the website without showing this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the Gateway's name, to the person who manages it. Don't change settings on a different Gateway; only the Gateway named in this task has browsing turned off.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Browser automation is explicitly disabled on the selected Gateway (GATEWAY_BROWSER_ENABLED=false), so readiness reports disabled before checking the browser backend.

What this means

  • Gateway browser readiness returns disabled when its configured browser-enabled flag is false, before checking the automation backend. Readiness describes the selected Gateway and does not grant execution permission. Settle active work before an operator restart, then refresh metadata for the intended new task.

Why this can happen

  • Gateway browser readiness returns disabled when its configured browser-enabled flag is false, before checking the automation backend.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect GATEWAY_BROWSER_ENABLED on that host and the refreshed Gateway readiness; conversation permission is a separate check.

How to fix it

  • The Gateway explicitly disables browser automation with GATEWAY_BROWSER_ENABLED=false. If browser use is intended, remove that opt-out or set it to true, restart the Gateway after active work is settled, and refresh metadata for a new task. Conversation permission alone does not change the Gateway setting.

Retry and execution caution

  • The selected Gateway enables browser automation and refreshed metadata advertises it.

How to verify the fix

  • After the operator changes the intended setting and safely restarts, refreshed readiness no longer reports disabled.

What not to do

  • Do not change another Gateway or treat conversation permission as a host configuration change.

Technical notes

  • Readiness describes the selected Gateway and does not grant execution permission. Settle active work before an operator restart, then refresh metadata for the intended new task.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
